parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A cell with internal resistance $r$ is connected to two resistors of resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ as shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1.png}}

Fig. 6.1

The potential differences (p.d.s) across $R_1$ and $R_2$ are $V_1$ and $V_2$ respectively.
The terminal p.d. across the cell is $V$.
The current in the circuit is $I$.

Use Kirchhoff's laws to show that the total resistance $R_T$ of the external circuit is given by

$$R_T = R_1 + R_2.$$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of the cell in Fig. 6.1 is $1.50\text{ V}$.

The values of $R_1$ and $R_2$ are $10\Omega$ and $15\Omega$ respectively. The terminal p.d. of the cell is $1.35\text{ V}$.

Calculate the internal resistance $r$ of the cell.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
A resistor of resistance $R_3$ is added to the circuit in Fig. 6.1, so that the circuit is as shown in Fig. 6.2.

{{figure:figure_6_2.png}}

Fig. 6.2

State and explain the effect, if any, of this change on:

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: the terminal p.d. of the cell.
